extracted.intended_audience: oil and gas industry operators, engineers, and air quality regulators (and stakeholders preparing regulatory comments)
extracted.subtask_short: oil and gas emissions reduction guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of recommended emission-reduction methods and how to evaluate them for oil & gas operations (compressors, dehydrators, pipelines, tanks, valves, wells, etc.), including estimated payback, capital cost categories, and sector applicability. Also includes an advocacy comment arguing EPA's proposed NSPS/NESHAP need strengthening to protect health and reduce methane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated Payback
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorizes emission-reduction measures by expected financial payback period: 0-1 year; 1-3 years; 3-10 years; >10 years; N/A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Natural Gas STAR summary groups each practice under an estimated payback column (examples: many compressor and valve measures show 0-1 year or 1-3 years; electric compressors often >10 years). Use payback category to prioritize low-cost/high-return measures first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital Cost Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Capital cost categories used for measures: < $1,000; $1,000 - $10,000; > $10,000; N/A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each recommended action in the table is assigned a capital cost bracket to help operators estimate upfront investment. Pair capital cost with estimated payback to assess economic feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector Applicability (Production / Gathering & Processing / Transmission & Distribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each measure the table indicates applicable segments by marking X under Production, Gathering & Processing, Transmission & Distribution (and sometimes more specific subcategories like Compressors/Engines, Tanks, Pipelines, Wells, Valves).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the applicability marks to determine which measures are relevant to a facility type or portion of the system. Many measures apply across multiple segments; others are segment-specific (e.g., glycol dehydrator measures apply to Production/Gathering & Processing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compressors / Engines — recommended measures
rubrics_metrics.description: List of practices to reduce compressor/engine emissions: Convert engine starting to nitrogen; Reduce the frequency of engine starts with gas; Replace gas starters with air; Replace ignition to reduce false starts; Automate systems operation to reduce venting; Replace compressor cylinder unloaders; Reduce methane emissions from compressor rod packing systems; Reduce emissions when taking compressors off-line; Redesign blowdown systems and alter ESD practices; Install electric starters; Automated air/fuel ratio controls; Replace wet seals with dry seals in centrifugal compressors; Lower purge pressure for shutdown controls; Install electric compressors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each measure is linked to a PRO Fact Sheet or Lessons Learned/Presentation (e.g., PRO Fact Sheet #101-#111, #110). The table shows estimated payback and capital cost ranges for each practice; e.g., many starter/automation changes show 0-1 or 1-3 year payback and <$1,000–$10,000 capital. Use referenced fact sheets for implementation details and case studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dehydrators — recommended measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures for glycol/desiccant dehydrators: Reroute glycol skimmer gas; Convert gas-driven chemical pumps to instrument air; Optimize glycol circulation and install flash tank separators; Pipe glycol dehydrator to vapor recovery unit; Replace glycol dehydration units with methanol injection; Zero emissions dehydrators; Portable desiccant dehydrators; Replace gas-assisted glycol pumps with electric pumps; Replace glycol dehydrators with desiccant dehydrators; Replace glycol dehydrator with separators and in-line heaters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact sheets #201-#207 and Lessons Learned provide technical guidance. Payback and cost vary by option (many dehydration optimizations show 0-3 year payback; some capital-intensive retrofits are 3-10+ years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pneumatics / Controls — recommended measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures to reduce emissions from pneumatic devices and controls: Convert pneumatics to mechanical controls; Reduce frequency of replacing turbine meter modules; Options for reducing methane emissions from pneumatic devices; Convert gas pneumatic controls to instrument air; Install electronic flare ignition devices; Replace bi-directional orifice metering with ultrasonic meters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced fact sheets include #301-#304. Many pneumatic-control conversions show low capital cost and short payback; other metering upgrades can be more costly. Consult Lessons Learned documents and presentations for implementation specifics and remote-site considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pipelines — recommended measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Pipeline-focused measures: Inject blowdown gas into low pressure mains; Composite wrap for non‑leaking pipeline defects; Insert gas main flexible liners; Use pipeline pump-down techniques to lower gas line pressure before maintenance; Install ejectors; Use hot taps for in‑service pipeline connections; Inspect flowlines annually; Use improved protective coating at canal crossings; Use inert gases and pigs to perform pipeline purges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact sheets #401-#407 and associated Lessons Learned/Presentations provide operational details. The table assigns payback and capital cost ranges to each measure to support prioritization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tanks — recommended measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures for storage and tanks: Purge and retire low pressure gasholders; Convert water tank blanket from natural gas to produced CO2; Consolidate crude oil production and water storage tanks; Install pressurized storage of condensate; Install vapor recovery units on crude oil storage tanks; Recover gas from pipeline pigging operations; Recycle line recover gas during condensate loading; Capture methane released from pipeline liquid storage tanks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact sheets #501-#507 and Lessons Learned/Presentations provide technical design and case studies. Some tank measures (vapor recovery) can have multi-year payback but substantially reduce emissions and VOCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valves (fugitives) — recommended measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Fugitive emissions control practices: Inspect and repair compressor station blowdown valves; Install BASO® valves; Install flow valves; Replace burst plates with secondary relief valves; Use ultrasound to identify leaks; Manage scrubber dump valves; Close main and unit valves prior to blowdown; Use rupture pin shutoff devices; Use YALE® closures for ESD testing; Perform leak repair during pipeline replacement; Test and repair pressure safety valves; Design isolation valves to minimize gas blowdown volumes; Move fire gates in to reduce venting at compressor stations; Test gate station pressure relief valves with nitrogen; Install excess flow valves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact sheets #601-#612 and partner updates give specific methods and equipment. Many valve/fugitive control measures are low capital with short payback (< $1,000 to $10,000), and DI&M (directed inspection & maintenance) is emphasized as a recurring practice to find and fix leaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wells — recommended measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellsite measures: Connect casing to vapor recovery unit; Gas well unloading time optimization; Install plunger lift systems; Install compressors to capture casinghead gas; Lower heater‑treater temperature; Reduce emission completions for hydraulically fractured wells; Install velocity tubing strings; Install downhole separator pumps; Use foaming agents; Install pumpjacks on low-water-production gas wells; Gas well 'smart' automation systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact sheets #701-#709 and Lessons Learned/Presentations provide operational details. Emission-completion reductions and capture systems can be highly effective for reducing methane, with varied payback depending on production characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other / Miscellaneous measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional opportunities: Install flares; Process optimization; Acid gas removal; Micro turbine generators; Eliminate unnecessary equipment/systems; Optimize operating pressures; Nitrogen rejection unit optimization; Conduct DI&M at remote sites; Increase walking survey frequency (from 5-to 3-year); DI&M at compressor stations, gas processing plants and booster stations; Require improvements in the quality of gas received from producers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures and program-level actions are documented in PRO fact sheets #901-#907, partner updates and presentations. Many focus on programmatic DI&M, monitoring, and systemic optimization rather than single-equipment retrofits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directed Inspection and Maintenance (DI&M) and Optical Imaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Use DI&M programs, including optical imaging and increased walking surveys, to identify and repair leaks across facilities (gate stations, compressor stations, processing plants, surface facilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple Partner Updates, Lessons Learned, presentations, and PRO fact sheets (e.g., DI&M resources, remote-site DI&M) are referenced. DI&M is shown as a cross-cutting practice with varying estimated paybacks and is recommended as recurring maintenance to capture fugitive emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PRO Fact Sheets / Lessons Learned / Presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each recommended practice links to implementation resources: PRO Fact Sheets (2-page technical summaries), Lessons Learned documents (detailed case studies), and presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact sheet numbers (e.g., PRO Fact Sheet #101-#111 for compressors, #201‑#207 for dehydrators, etc.) are provided in the table. Users are directed to these resources (PDFs, presentations) for specifics on design, costs, implementation steps, and case examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy point: EPA NSPS/NESHAP proposed rules need strengthening
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRDC-led comment argues that while EPA’s proposed NSPS and NESHAP for the oil and gas industry make important steps to reduce smog-forming pollution and toxics, they 'do not go far enough' to protect public health and welfare and should be strengthened to reduce methane and local air pollution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit policy/evaluation criterion for a regulatory comment: commenters should identify where proposed rules are insufficient, quantify or describe public health and environmental harms (smog, toxic air contaminants, methane greenhouse impact), and urge EPA to adopt stronger standards. Use supporting technical measures (from the Natural Gas STAR summary) to recommend concrete regulatory or BACT/MACT/NSPS provisions.
